attributes.residual: STILL ONE OVER at T76/O77, and the extra instruction is still the duplicate zero. Re-derived from the aligned view at 0x44:0xa0: retail materialises zero ONCE (`li r20,0` at +0x60) and spends that same r20 for the word stores, for BOTH `stb` writes into label[], and as the source of two copies (`addi r19,r20,0` = slot, `addi r23,r20,0` = pieceoff). We still emit a second `li` for the byte value (r30 before this edit, r21 after it), and still remat `li r19,0` / `li r23,0` instead of copying. The consequence is a register-budget one: retail's thirteen callee-saved homes hold thirteen values, ours hold FOURTEEN because the byte zero is one of them, which is why our group4Base is pushed into volatile r4 while retail keeps it in r30. So the char-typed zero improved the colouring around the split without removing the split itself. Two levers remain untried and both are non-spelling: (a) the inner-loop index strength reduction the prior record named -- retail keeps handleoff as a live index (`stwx r3,r30,r24` with `addi r24,r24,4`) while MWCC strength-reduces ours to a walked pointer r31 -- with claim.law.recomputed-index-array-form-safe.20260831.v2 as the screened but still unprobed counter-form; (b) reducing the live-value count by one so the byte zero has somewhere to go without displacing group4Base.
